entry.title: Youtube adblocker that fixes video buffering - IframeTube
entry.summary:
Hello everyone, I have recently made an adblocker called IframeTube, which fixes all of Youtube video buffering, removes all ads, and returns the old player UI. It should be used in a combination with a second adblock (e.g. uBlock Origin) to work properly. It does this by using the embedded Youtube player, which is lightweight, has no ads, and includes the old UI. You can learn more about this in the README file of the repository. The project is completely free and open source. Features: no ads, no video buffering
old Youtube player ui
auto sets your preferred video quality
removes annoying shorts elements (optional)
lightweight
All your favorite features in the embedded player were remade: theater mode, Picture In Picture, autoplay & autoplay button
previous and next buttons with previews for the videos & next video preview is also available for non playlists videos, replay feature for the previous button
double speed logic activated when you hold space or left click on the video for 0.5s
playlist functionality
language based (the players tooltips, settings options are in your current language)
all shortcuts are supported
works perfectly with Youtube’s single page application
Download links: Chrome: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/iframetube-youtube-adbloc/popbfaalnmahdonefnbbogalimefpcnm Firefox: https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/iframetube-youtube-adblocker/ please note that firefox may include a bit more bugs, so if you find any, please open an issue on Github :) Issues, source code, more detailed explanation: https://github.com/IframeTube/IframeTube I hope this will solve your Youtube issues and make you enjoy Youtube again :). As I said, if you have any issues or questions, open an issue on Github. You can also donate if you like to support the development :) Thank you!

entry.title: YAGNI: The Principle That Protects You From Building the Future Too Early
entry.summary: Most developers don’t struggle with laziness. They struggle with imagination. We imagine scale. And that’s exactly where YAGNI comes in. YAGNI stands for: You Aren’t Gonna Need It The rule is brutally simple: If you don’t need it now, don’t build it now. Not “just in case”. YAGNI was introduced as part of Extreme Programming (XP) in the late 1990s by Kent Beck. Extreme Programming challenged traditional software thinking: Deliver fast Iterate often Refactor constantly Avoid speculative design Instead of predicting every future scenario, XP embraced incremental evolution. YAGNI became one of its core disciplines. Not because future-proofing is bad. But because speculative complexity is expensive. Most violations of YAGNI look intelligent. entry.title: I Launched a SaaS, Forgot About It, Then Discovered People Were Paying for a Broken Product
entry.summary: When I started making music videos for Youtube, I kept running into the same problem: manually timing lyrics took forever. Upload song. Listen on repeat. Note when each line starts. Export subtitle file. Adjust timing. Repeat. At least an hour per video. After doing this dozens of times, I thought there has to be a better way. So I built one. Then I forgot about it. I spent a few weeks building an MVP. Bought a domain. Deployed it. Then moved on to a different idea. entry.title: The Senior Engineer's Career Trap: Why You're Optimizing for the Wrong Thing
entry.summary: There's a pattern I've watched repeat itself more times than I can count. A talented developer spends three to four years grinding through difficult problems, earns the "Senior Engineer" title, gets a meaningful pay bump — and then stalls. Not because they stop learning. Not because they stop shipping. They stall because they keep doing exactly what got them promoted in the first place: writing good code, fixing hard bugs, unblocking teammates.
